The study used Barium M-Hexaferrite doped with Zn2+ at x=0.9 as the magnetic material component
Polyaniline doped with DBSA was used as the dielectric material component
The electrical conductivity of Polyaniline was 4.4 × 10⁻¹ S/m
The electrical conductivity of Barium M-Hexaferrite was 2.09 × 10⁻³ S/m
Both materials were classified as semiconductor materials with conductivity between 10⁻⁸ and 10³ S/m
The maximum reflection loss achieved was -29.6003 dB in variation D
Variation D achieved 96.69% energy absorption of incident electromagnetic waves
The minimum reflection loss was -15.2937 dB in variation A
Variation A achieved 82.21% energy absorption
The most effective absorption bandwidth was 1.81 GHz in variation D
The absorption bandwidth for variation D covered frequencies from 8 to 9.81 GHz
Plain steel with Agatha paint achieved only -3.7458 dB reflection loss and 34.68% energy absorption
The reflection coefficient for variation D was 0.0331, meaning 3.31% reflection
Zn2+ doping reduced the coercivity field (Hc) to 0.0181 Tesla
The maximum magnetization of Zn2+-doped Barium M-Hexaferrite was ~52.9 emu/g
The remanence magnetization (Mr) was ~15.86 emu/g for the Zn2+-doped material
The XRD analysis showed 67.33% Barium M-Hexaferrite dominant phase
The XRD analysis showed 32.67% Hematite (Fe₂O₃) secondary phase
The Goodness of Fit (GoF) value for Rietica refinement was 1.24
Barium M-Hexaferrite without doping had a coercivity field of ~0.1734 Tesla
Barium M-Hexaferrite with Zn2+ doping at x=0.3 had a coercivity field of ~0.0506 Tesla
The microwave absorption testing was conducted at 8-12 GHz frequency range (X-band)
The double-layer coating design used variations of PANi and PANi + BaM layers
The composition ratio of PANi : (PANi + BaM) was 3:1 for the most effective variation
Iron ore from Tanah Laut, South Kalimantan was used as the source material for Fe3+ ions
